object_types.name: Vendor
object_types.definition: A supplier record in the supplier master, onboarded and used by procurement for purchasing goods/services.

source_references.excerpt: The vendor record. It's the thing in the supplier master.
Oh. Vendor number. Every vendor has a vendor number, it's generated when the record is created.

object_types.definition: The unique identifier of a vendor record.

source_references.excerpt: Oh. Vendor number. Every vendor has a vendor number, it's generated when the record is created.
It's the primary key. It's been the primary key since before I got here.

object_types.name: VendorStatus
object_types.definition: The current lifecycle status of a vendor.

source_references.excerpt: Draft, active, suspended.
Collapsed into three, yes. Draft, active, suspended. That's what the field allows now. Every vendor is in exactly one of them.

object_types.name: SpendTier
object_types.definition: Procurement's classification of a vendor based on spend volume.

source_references.excerpt: Every vendor has a tier. Bronze, silver, gold.
I'm talking about spend. Gold vendors are the ones we spend real money with, they get quarterly business reviews, better payment terms, a named relationship manager.

object_types.name: RiskTier
object_types.definition: Compliance's classification of a vendor's risk level, set by the review.

source_references.excerpt: I use low, medium, high.
And I'm talking about risk. Low, medium, high, based on the review -- what data they touch, what geography they operate in, whether they're a sole source.

object_types.name: RiskReview
object_types.definition: A record of a compliance risk review for a vendor, of which at most one is current/signed-off.

source_references.excerpt: The review is its own record. It has a review ID, because we need to know who signed it and when, and auditors ask. It's not a checkbox on the vendor.
A vendor accumulates review records over time. At most one is the current one. Being active requires a current signed-off review.

ambiguities.description: Vendor addresses: three distinct addresses (remit-to, ship-from, legal) are mentioned but not modeled as separate fact types/value types since the level of structure (single text field vs. structured street/city/etc.) and their exact fact-type relationships were not clarified in the session. Should each address type be its own value type or entity, and how granular should the structure be?

source_references.excerpt: Address, though we have three addresses really -- remit-to, ship-from, and the legal one, which are frequently different and frequently wrong.

ambiguities.description: The 'current' / 'signed-off' status of a RiskReview is discussed extensively (at most one current review per vendor, must be signed off) but no explicit field/value type for 'current' or 'signed-off' flag was captured in the model. Should RiskReview have a boolean/status attribute (e.g., IsCurrent, SignedOffBy/SignedOffDate) to support the 'at most one current' and 'active requires current signed-off review' constraints?

source_references.excerpt: A vendor can have several reviews over its life -- we re-review on a cycle, and every re-review is a new record, we don't edit the old one. But one of them is the current signed-off one.
Every _active_ vendor has a current signed-off review. A draft vendor has no review at all

ambiguities.description: The rule 'a vendor cannot be moved to active without a completed/current signed-off risk review' is a mandatory/subset-style constraint conditioned on VendorStatus='active', which the current fact-type model (Vendor has VendorStatus / RiskReview belongs to Vendor) cannot fully express without an explicit 'current review' attribute. Should this be modeled as a subtype (ActiveVendor) with mandatory current-review, or via a derived/conditional constraint?

source_references.excerpt: Every active vendor has exactly one completed risk review. ... A vendor accumulates review records over time. At most one is the current one. Being active requires a current signed-off review.

ambiguities.description: Vendor Tier naming collision: both procurement and compliance call their classification 'tier', causing organizational confusion. The model resolves this by naming them SpendTier and RiskTier as distinct fields, per Mei's confirmation, but the transcript indicates this naming split is not actually adopted in practice organization-wide -- is 'tier' used elsewhere in the system/reports in a way that could still cause ambiguity?

source_references.excerpt: And you both call it "tier." ... We've asked people to say spend tier and risk tier. Nobody does. It's been a losing battle for two years. ... No. Two separate fields, different values, different owners.

ambiguities.description: Post-suspension handling of in-flight Purchase Orders (a potential 'run-off' status) is explicitly parked/undecided pending the steering group and Legal. No constraint or additional VendorStatus value was added for this, per explicit instruction not to model it yet. Should a placeholder status or fact type be added once policy is decided?

source_references.excerpt: Today's model captures three statuses and the creation-time control, and nothing about post-suspension fulfilment, because there is nothing agreed to capture.

ambiguities.description: The 'preferred vendor' flag mentioned by Mei (an informal spreadsheet column indicating preference when multiple vendors supply the same item) was explicitly excluded from the model as ad hoc with no defined rule. Confirm this remains out of scope, or if a future defined rule should be captured.

source_references.excerpt: There's a column called "preferred." ... It's ad hoc. Don't model it.

ambiguities.description: Vendor duplicate records (same tax ID, same company onboarded twice) are a known data quality/compliance issue but no de-duplication or merge process is modeled. Is this out of scope entirely, or does the model need a way to represent 'merged into' relationships between vendor records?

source_references.excerpt: We have vendors with the same tax ID -- different legal entities under one parent that file together, or we've onboarded the same company twice by accident and nobody's merged them.
The duplicates are also a compliance problem, for what it's worth. If we've got the same entity twice we can't see aggregate exposure.

ambiguities.description: Temporal/history tracking: Vendor status, tiers, and contacts appear to change over time (e.g., regional sourcing change caused contact model to shift), but the model as captured represents only current-state facts. Should status/tier/contact history be tracked explicitly (e.g., effective dates) given the audit and compliance context?

source_references.excerpt: Since we went to regional sourcing last year, it's one primary contact per region.
A vendor can have several reviews over its life -- we re-review on a cycle, and every re-review is a new record, we don't edit the old one.
